evals.prompt: We're Tallowmere, 25 people, building speech models. Our Hugging Face org `tallowmere` is on the free plan. Next Tuesday we open-source Tallow-ASR in tiny/small/medium plus a GGUF build. Plan: one repo `tallowmere/tallow-asr` with a subfolder per size and the GGUF in /gguf, weights are the pytorch_model.bin files from training. We also want a Gradio demo Space under the org so people can try it. To get on trending fast we'll raffle three RTX cards among everyone who likes the repo in launch week. Can you write the launch checklist?
evals.expected_output: A release plan that splits the variants into one repo each linked by base_model and grouped in a collection, converts pickle weights to safetensors, flags that a free org cannot create a Gradio Space and offers Static or a paid plan, refuses the like raffle as restricted metric manipulation, and gives a dated cadence.
expectations: Recommends one Hub repository per size (tiny, small, medium) instead of subfolders in a single repo
Recommends a separate repository for the GGUF build
Sets base_model (with base_model_relation quantized or equivalent) on the GGUF repo card pointing at the original model repo
Recommends grouping the repos in a Hugging Face collection
States that subfolders inside one repo lose separate URLs, search entries or download counts
States that pickle .bin weights trigger import-scan warnings on the Hub page and recommends safetensors
States that a free organization cannot create a Gradio (compute) Space and needs a paid plan such as Team
Offers a Static Space (e.g. in-browser via transformers.js or ONNX) or a plan upgrade as the demo path
Cites Hugging Face's Content Policy wording on incentivizing metric manipulation or exchanging rewards for likes when refusing the raffle
Names a sanction such as unranking or removal for metric manipulation
Proposes driving real visits to the model page instead of rewarded likes
Lists card metadata fields to fill before launch, including at least pipeline_tag, library_name and license
Includes a dated cadence that flips repos public together on launch day and staffs the Community tab
Does not set base_model between the independently trained sizes (tiny, small, medium)

evals.prompt: Our sales VP at Brightwell Data wants every download of our open embedding model (Apache-2.0) to become a lead. Plan is to turn on gated access with manual approval and ask for company, job title, phone and team size, then SDRs approve the good ones and reject students. We release in two weeks on HF. How should I set up the gate?
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on a lead-capture gate: grants are per user not per company, manual approval adds a queue, rejection is permanent, PII responsibility; recommends open or click-through gate and a commercial link in the card for leads, ranked with adoption vs compliance cost.
expectations: Recommends an open repo or an automatic-approval click-through gate instead of manual approval for this Apache-2.0 model
States that Hugging Face grants gated access to individual users, not to whole companies
Points out that every engineer and CI job at an adopting company would need its own approved account or token
States that rejected users cannot request access again
States that gating shares requesters' username and email by default and makes the publisher responsible for that personal data
Mentions linking or publishing a privacy policy or notice if personal data is collected
Presents gate options ordered by adoption cost (open first, manual or external approval last)
Includes a compliance or legal cost dimension in the comparison
Recommends capturing sales interest via a link in the model card or pinned FAQ to the company's own form
Mentions that username and email collection can be turned off in the gating settings
Does not provide an extra_gated_fields block asking for phone number as the recommended configuration

evals.prompt: Board deck question. Our model page on Hugging Face shows 2.1M downloads last month, our Python SDK on PyPI had 310k. I want to put 'Monthly active developers: 2.4M' on the slide. Also marketing says the launch flopped because the model only got 140 likes, versus 3,000+ for the big lab releases. Can you sanity check before Thursday?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to sum Hub and PyPI downloads or call them active developers; explains Hub counting (GET/HEAD on query file, not deduplicated); explains likes and downloads measure different things; proposes separate lines and derivative count; names Publisher Analytics / unique downloader limits.
expectations: States that Hub downloads count requests on query files rather than people, so 2.1M cannot be read as developers
States that Hub and PyPI download counts use different counting rules and cannot be summed
Explains that a Hub download is a GET or HEAD request on a query file such as config.json
States that Hub download counts are not deduplicated by user
Mentions that clones, CI runs or cache misses can inflate the download count
Explains that likes and downloads measure different things (attention to new releases vs ongoing pipeline usage)
Does not conclude the launch failed from the like count alone
Proposes reporting likes, downloads and other numbers as separate lines with their counting rules
Proposes derivatives in the model tree (fine-tunes, quantizations, adapters) as an adoption signal
States that unique downloader data is only available as a paid Enterprise-tier log export or similar paid analytics
Suggests a defensible replacement slide label such as 'Hub downloads (non-deduplicated)'

evals.prompt: We're Lumière Labs in Lyon. We trained a 7B text-generation model from scratch, about 3e23 FLOP. License: our 'Lumière Open License', free for companies under $5M revenue, paid above, and no use for military purposes. Marketing wants to announce it as 'fully open source' on Hugging Face and legal assumed the AI Act open-source exemption covers us so we skip the paperwork. What do I put in the card and are we good?
evals.expected_output: Says the model likely meets the GPAI indicative test, the open-source exemption likely does not apply because of monetisation and use restrictions, copyright policy and training-data summary apply regardless, sets license other + license_name + license_link, avoids 'open source' wording, routes to counsel.
expectations: States the model likely falls under the EU AI Act general-purpose AI model obligations (training compute above about 1e23 FLOP and generates text)
States that the open-source exemption requires a free and open-source license without monetisation
Concludes the paid-above-$5M term likely disqualifies the exemption
States that a copyright policy is required even for exempt open-source models
States that a public training-data summary (on the AI Office template) is required even for exempt open-source models
Mentions the 2 August 2025 application date of the obligations
Notes the systemic-risk threshold (around 1e25 FLOP) is not reached at 3e23
Sets license: other with license_name and license_link (or a LICENSE file) in the card metadata
Lists what the open-source exemption covers: technical documentation for authorities, documentation for downstream providers, and the EU authorised representative
Recommends linking the training-data summary and copyright policy from the model card
Mentions that the Commission enforces the GPAI obligations, including fines, from 2 August 2026

evals.prompt: Our model `kestrel-ai/kestrel-vision-2b` has been on the Hub for three weeks and the page still has no 'Inference' box where people can try it like the big models do. Our CEO asked me to just enable the HF inference API on it before the webinar on the 12th. Where's the setting?
evals.expected_output: Explains there is no owner setting: widgets appear only when an Inference Provider serves the model and providers choose what they deploy; offers ask-for-provider-support, widget example outputs in card YAML, a linked Space demo, and self-hosting via Inference Endpoints; does not promise a widget by the webinar.
expectations: States there is no setting a model owner can toggle to enable the inference widget
States the widget appears only when at least one Inference Provider serves the model
States that Inference Providers decide themselves which models they deploy
Recommends the 'Ask for provider support' request on the model page
Recommends adding example outputs to the card via the widget YAML metadata
Recommends a Space demo linked to the model (models: in the Space README) as the try-it path for the webinar
Mentions checking whether the org plan allows a Gradio Space or using a Static Space
Mentions self-hosting (e.g. Inference Endpoints, TGI or vLLM) as a fallback
Does not promise the widget will be live by the webinar date
Checks or mentions that correct pipeline_tag and model metadata are prerequisites for a widget

evals.prompt: Quick one: our paper went on arXiv on Sept 30 and we launch the model on HF Oct 20. Today is Oct 18. I want to submit it to Daily Papers on launch day for the bump. Also our org is on Team, and for the ZeroGPU demo I set @spaces.GPU(duration=300) everywhere just to be safe since generation takes ~20 seconds. Anything else I should do in the last 48 hours?
evals.expected_output: Flags the closed Daily Papers window (14 days after arXiv date), keeps the arxiv link in the card; tells them to set duration to realistic worst case because declared duration is checked against visitor quota; gives a compressed 48-hour checklist.
expectations: States the Daily Papers window closes 14 days after the arXiv publication date
Concludes the Sept 30 paper can no longer be submitted on Oct 20
Recommends still linking the arXiv paper in the model card so the Hub creates the arxiv tag and paper-page cross-link
States that the declared ZeroGPU duration is checked against the visitor's remaining daily quota
Explains that duration=300 would lock out free or anonymous visitors whose daily quota is only a few minutes
Recommends setting duration close to the realistic worst case (for example around 30-60 seconds for a ~20 s task)
Mentions that a shorter declared duration also improves queue priority
Includes testing the usage snippet in a clean environment before flipping public
Includes linking the Space to the model repo via models: in the Space README
Includes staffing the Community tab on launch day
Gives a compressed checklist adapted to the 48 hours left rather than a multi-week plan
States that the 14-day window counts from the paper's first arXiv version and a new version does not reopen it

evals.prompt: We're Harrowgate Voice, a US startup (Delaware, Austin office). We're putting our 3B text-to-speech model on Hugging Face next month, Apache-2.0, trained with roughly 2e23 FLOP. Our counsel says the EU AI Act is irrelevant because we have no EU customers and TTS isn't a 'general-purpose' chatbot anyway. To be extra safe they want us to turn on the EU block in the gating settings and call it done. Can you confirm and give me the card checklist?
evals.expected_output: Corrects both premises: audio generation is inside the Commission's modality test, and a public Hub release places the model on the EU market; Apache-2.0 likely qualifies for the open-source exemption but copyright policy and training-data summary still apply; EU IP block is not an AI Act opt-out and gating hurts adoption; card checklist with metadata and links.
expectations: States the Commission's indicative test covers models that generate language including audio, so a text-to-speech model is inside the modality test
States that 2e23 FLOP is above the roughly 1e23 FLOP indicative threshold
States that a public Hugging Face repo downloadable from the EU places the model on the EU market regardless of customer location
States that the extra_gated_eu_disallowed EU block is not an AI Act exemption or opt-out
States that the EU block only works on gated repos, so it would force a gate on an Apache-2.0 model
Concludes the Apache-2.0 release likely qualifies for the open-source exemption if weights and usage information are public and it is not systemic-risk
States the copyright policy obligation still applies under the exemption
States the public training-data summary still applies under the exemption
Mentions that a non-EU provider outside the exemption would need an EU authorised representative
Includes pipeline_tag text-to-speech and library_name in the card metadata checklist
Recommends linking the training-data summary and copyright policy from the model card
Recommends counsel re-check the conclusion given the corrected premises
Notes that a lack-of-significant-generality argument, not customer location, is the only premise of counsel's position worth documenting
